message.content:
Introduction

Artificial intelligence (AI) has expanded from narrow symbolic systems into a broad field of data-driven models, learning algorithms, and decision-support technologies. This paper investigates the methodological foundations of modern AI by linking model design, empirical evaluation, and institutional governance. To make the paper’s hierarchy of analysis explicit, we use the following nested notation: ( ( ( ( ( [ [ [ [ [ { { { { { core } } } } } ] ] ] ] ] ) ) ) ) ).

The “core” term denotes the central technical claim that AI systems can learn representations from data, while the surrounding layers mark, in turn, the dataset, architecture, training procedure, benchmark, and policy context under which such claims are assessed. We argue that responsible AI research requires explicit attention to each level of this hierarchy, because errors, biases, and uncertainties propagate across technical and social boundaries.

The remainder of this paper proceeds as follows. Section 2 reviews the relevant literature. Section 3 presents the conceptual framework. Section 4 discusses empirical examples and limitations. Section 5 concludes with recommendations for future research.
